knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Find the **exact** value of the expression below.

$$
\cos\left(105^\circ\right)\cos\left(30^\circ\right)+\sin\left(105^\circ\right)\sin\left(30^\circ\right)
$$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recognize the difference formula in reverse:

$$
\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y=\cos(x-y).
$$

Combining the angles gives

$$
\cos\left(105^\circ-30^\circ\right)=\cos\left(75^\circ\right).
$$

Choose a decomposition into special angles:

$$
75^\circ=300^\circ-225^\circ.
$$

Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(75^\circ\right)=\cos\left(300^\circ-225^\circ\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(300^\circ\right)\cos\left(225^\circ\right)+\sin\left(300^\circ\right)\sin\left(225^\circ\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)+\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\
&=\frac{- \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: real fixed angles; exact radical arithmetic

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Find the **exact** value of the expression below.

$$
\cos\left(285^\circ\right)\cos\left(60^\circ\right)-\sin\left(285^\circ\right)\sin\left(60^\circ\right)
$$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recognize the sum formula in reverse:

$$
\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y=\cos(x+y).
$$

Combining the angles gives

$$
\cos\left(285^\circ+60^\circ\right)=\cos\left(345^\circ\right).
$$

Choose a decomposition into special angles:

$$
345^\circ=135^\circ+210^\circ.
$$

Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(345^\circ\right)=\cos\left(135^\circ+210^\circ\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(135^\circ\right)\cos\left(210^\circ\right)-\sin\left(135^\circ\right)\sin\left(210^\circ\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \left(- \frac{1}{2}\right) \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right) \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: real fixed angles; exact radical arithmetic

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Find the **exact** value of the expression below.

$$
\cos\left(-\frac{19\pi}{12}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(-\frac{19\pi}{12}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
$$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recognize the sum formula in reverse:

$$
\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y=\cos(x+y).
$$

Combining the angles gives

$$
\cos\left(-\frac{19\pi}{12}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\cos\left(-\frac{17\pi}{12}\right).
$$

Choose a decomposition into special angles:

$$
-\frac{17\pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{7\pi}{4}.
$$

Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(-\frac{17\pi}{12}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{7\pi}{4}\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\sin\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\right) \\
&=\frac{- \sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: real fixed angles; exact radical arithmetic

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Find the **exact** value of the expression below.

$$
\cos\left(\frac{23\pi}{12}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{23\pi}{12}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)
$$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recognize the difference formula in reverse:

$$
\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y=\cos(x-y).
$$

Combining the angles gives

$$
\cos\left(\frac{23\pi}{12}-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{19\pi}{12}\right).
$$

Choose a decomposition into special angles:

$$
\frac{19\pi}{12}=\frac{5\pi}{6}+\frac{3\pi}{4}.
$$

Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(\frac{19\pi}{12}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}+\frac{3\pi}{4}\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\
&=\frac{- \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$
